output.summary: KEP-2291 proposed letting Prow read optional presubmit job definitions from a prow.yaml file inside the tested repository, instead of only from the central infra-config repo. The KEP reached status implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Presubmits lived only in the central infra-config repo, so a PR adding or changing a presubmit could not be verified in that PR, and branch copies had to be maintained by hand. The proposal makes in-repo presubmit configuration optional and opt-in, and has Prow components fetch it through a git client. Non-public test-infra repos also blocked outside collaborators from changing job configs, which this addresses.

alternatives.option: Keep all presubmits in the central infra-config repository
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as the source of the problems: a new presubmit cannot be verified in the PR that introduces it, and branch copies must be maintained manually.

alternatives.option: Configure Postsubmits or Periodics inside the tested repository as well
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this under Non-Goals and says it may be done in a future iteration.

evidence.quote: This document proposes to change the Prow presubmit handling to optionally version some or all presubmits in the same repository that also contains the code that is being tested.
It is not possible to see in a Pull Request that introduces a new presubmit if that presubmit will actually pass.
This feature is optional and opt-in
The option to configure Postsubmits or Periodics inside the tested repository. This may be done in a future iteration.
